chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the doubter and the disobedient one are in the Fire; they are neither from us nor to us.

key_terms.إِلَيْنَا: To us (returning to us/connected to us)
key_terms.الشَّكَّ: Doubt (specifically spiritual doubt or doubt in faith)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by saying the doubter and disobedient are 'neither from us nor to us'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual state of doubt (shakk) directly to disobedience (ma'siyah), presenting it as a distinct cause for Hellfire. By declaring that those possessing these traits are 'neither from us nor to us,' he establishes a criterion of spiritual genealogy, separating the Ahl al-Bayt from those whose internal uncertainty manifests in external disobedience. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the unity of knowledge, conviction, and action, where doubt is not merely an intellectual state but a spiritual defect leading to separation from the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The doubter and the disobedient one would be in the Fire. He is neither from us<sup>asws</sup> nor to us<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Doubts and disobedience are in the fire. It (doubt or people having doubts) is not from us nor is it directed to us.’”
